subject: Integrated lighting and accessory storage
hook: Wardrobe lighting has to be planned before the build, not added after.
ig:
Wardrobe lighting has to be planned before the build, not added after.

Once a wardrobe is assembled, hiding cables neatly gets much harder. So these decisions come first:

Where the light goes. Lighting the front of the rail shows your clothes; a strip behind it mostly lights the back panel.

How it switches. Door sensor, motion sensor or switch, each routed differently.

Where the power comes from. We plan hidden routes through the carcass at design stage; a qualified electrician makes the connection.

Then the accessory storage that stops wardrobes turning into a jumble:

- A shallow drawer with dividers for watches, jewellery and cufflinks
- Pull-out shoe shelves at a height you can see
- Trouser, tie and belt racks where you actually reach

Save this for your wardrobe plans, and see our fitted wardrobes through the link in bio.
fb:
If you'd like lights in a new wardrobe, now's the time to say so, not after it's built.

We plan where the light goes (ideally lighting the clothes, not the back wall), how it switches on, and how cables run hidden through the units, so a qualified electrician can simply connect it. While we're at it, we'll plan the small stuff: a divided drawer for jewellery and watches, pull-out shoe shelves, and racks for belts and ties.

Have a look at our fitted wardrobes for ideas.

on_asset:
S1: Light it, organise it, plan it first / Six decisions for a better wardrobe |
S2: Light the front of the rail — A strip behind the rail lights the back wall. Lighting from the front or top lights the clothes you're choosing. |
S3: Choose how it switches on — Door sensor, motion sensor or switch. Each needs a different route for cables, so decide early. |
S4: Plan the power route — Where the supply comes from and how cables run hidden through the carcass. Your electrician connects it. |
S5: A drawer for small things — A shallow drawer with dividers for watches, jewellery and belts saves a deep drawer becoming a jumble. |
S6: Pull-outs where you reach — Shoe shelves, trouser rails and tie or belt racks work best at the heights you actually use. |
S7: Light, switch, power, drawers, pull-outs — Save this before your consultation. Link in bio. |
